claims.text: The starting material is an equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
Carbide-forming elements are to be added to the CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
Adding carbide-forming elements will increase the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi.
Adding carbide-forming elements will increase the strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
The modification will retain the favorable mechanical characteristics of the original alloy.
Ball milling is an applicable solid-state synthesis step for the proposed modification.
High-temperature spark plasma sintering is an applicable consolidation step for the proposed modification.
The intervention will form high-entropy carbides within the modified CoCrFeNiTi material.
The resulting high-entropy carbides will have a rock-salt fcc structure.
The entropy-forming-ability descriptor predicts the synthesizability of disordered five-metal refractory carbides as homogeneous high-entropy single phases.
Formation of homogeneous high-entropy carbide phases will cause increased hardness in the modified alloy.
Formation of homogeneous high-entropy carbide phases will cause increased strength in the modified alloy.
The original CoCrFeNiTi baseline is without carbide-forming elements.
The required amount of added carbide-forming elements is uncertain.
The optimal processing conditions are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as being without carbide-forming elements even though the stated CoCrFeNiTi composition contains Ti, itself a carbide-forming element. The intended distinction may be 'without additional carbide-forming elements,' but that is not what the baseline states.
